thread:
Maria: Heads-up — noticed a spike in late telemetry for US-EAST between 03:00-05:00 UTC, batches missing ~2h of events for some tenants.
Liam: thanks. any pattern on tenant size or ingesters?
Devon: most are small tenants, but a couple mid-size ones hit a delayed shard reattach. likely downstream kafka lag.
Maria: I'm thinking we run a targeted backfill for affected partitions instead of a full recompute. lower blast radius.
Ashley: +1 for targeted. we need quota gating so reprocess doesn't starve realtime. can we run under low-priority lane? :thinking_face:
Liam: routing-wise we already have a priority-lane flag on the replay API. question is whether console should expose a preflight estimate for token-hours and peak concurrency. ops team wants that.
Devon: preflight estimate is tricky — depends on dedupe hit rate. rough numbers: 120k events, avg 250ms per event on dedicated worker => ~8.3h total if sequential, but with batching we can do in ~1.2h @ 8 workers. Cost est: ~0.6 worker-hours per tenant.
Maria: can you paste the CLI we used to run the dry-run? saves time for SRE.
Devon: sure:
```
# dry-run to estimate shapes
replayctl run --project prod --shards 3 --dry-run --from 2026-03-19T03:00Z --to 2026-03-19T05:00Z --target-lane low
```
Ashley: ops-bot reported one early failure on a different job earlier today. need backoff + idempotency check in replay worker. ops-bot: job 872 exited 2 (checkpoint write failure) — retry scheduled.
ops-bot: job 872 retry 1 started by ashleys-replay-agent.
Liam: infra note — if we throttle too low, prefix KV cache misses will spike and realtime latency suffers. we should cap concurrent replayers per shard to 2 and enable local prefix-cache warmup.
Devon: ack. will add --concurrency 2 and a warmup pass before replay. also adding a dedupe-tier param to skip obvious duplicates for small tenants: `--dedupe-level light`.
Maria: UX ask: can we add a single checkbox in Console "Show preflight cost & runtime estimate" that triggers the dry-run and returns numbers (and an opt-in for running under low priority)? keeps rollout minimal.
Liam: API debate: exposing dry-run via public API (replay.preflight) vs keeping it internal only to console. security/compliance prefers internal only for now.
Devon: internal-only is fine — we can still return structured estimate JSON to the console so it shows cost and walltime. sample response: `{\n  "events": 118234,\n  "estimated_worker_hours": 0.72,\n  "wall_time_minutes": 78,\n  "peak_concurrency": 6\n}`
Ashley: add SLO guard: if estimated_worker_hours > 10 or peak_concurrency > 50, require a manual approval flow and create an incident ticket.
Maria: agreed. also let's add a short runbook blurb in Console UI near the action: "If job touches >3 partitions, contact infra".
Liam: scheduling note — we'll route replays to eu-west as failover only; primary will stay us-east for data locality.
Devon: I'll open a tiny RFC for the replay preflight endpoint + console checkbox and include the CLI snippets and warmup + idempotency checklist.
Maria: can you include a one-click escalate link to create a temporary quota bump if the preflight shows a >5x cost spike?
Ashley: SRE + oncall will own the approval workflow. I'll draft the PagerDuty runbook once RFC lands.
Devon: launching a dry-run now against tenant t-42, will post results in ~20m.
ops-bot: dry-run 873 started by devon (dry-run id=873).
Maria: thanks — ping in thread with the numbers and then we can ship the console change behind a feature flag. :rocket:
